safety_verdicts.content: Patient has a 5-day history of feeling generally unwell with cough and cold symptoms.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated facts note a flu-like illness/SOB but do not document a 5-day duration or the presence of cough/cold symptoms.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Omitting the 5-day duration and cough/cold features reduces the clinical context needed to gauge trajectory (early vs prolonged illness) and to differentiate viral URI/flu from evolving bacterial infection. This can modestly affect diagnostic reasoning and appropriateness of antibiotics or follow-up timing.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: No generated fact describes the cough or that it is mainly dry.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Not documenting that the cough is mainly dry removes a helpful discriminator between uncomplicated viral illness and productive cough syndromes (e.g., pneumonia/bronchitis). This is unlikely to directly cause harm but can lead to less accurate assessment and monitoring advice.

safety_verdicts.content: Patient reports feeling hot/cold and sweaty, but has had no fevers.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated facts include hot/cold and sweating, but do not include the gold detail that there were no fevers.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Failing to record that there were no fevers (despite sweats/hot-cold sensations) may overstate infection severity and could bias toward unnecessary antibiotics or escalation. However, the presence/absence of measured fever is only one element and typically causes limited harm on its own.
